lots.title: (1) Tomintoul 1967 Silvano's Collection 50 Year Old 50th Anniversary Single Malt Scotch Whisky, 45.2% ABV (GB)
lots.what_it_really_is: Masam (Maryse Accorsi Samaroli) Silvano's Collection Tomintoul 1967, 50 years old, bottled 2018 for the 1968-2018 Samaroli anniversary, casks 4688 and 5425, 45.2%, 70cl, in wooden box with brass plate and signed neck tag. Release size of 180 bottles comes from the Sotheby's lot page, not the photos.
lots.what_the_title_misses: Only the Samaroli/Masam name, the cask numbers (4688 and 5425), the 2018 bottling year and 70cl. The title already names the vintage, age, 50th Anniversary and Silvano's Collection, which is the bottle's own name, so collectors searching for it will find it. Gap is cosmetic, not hidden value.
lots.photo_evidence: Re-read all 3 photos and enlarged the neck label from photo 1 (4x crop). Read clearly: '1968 ANNIVERSARY 2018', large gold '50', 'YEARS OLD', '...Malt Scotch Whisky', '1967 Tomintoul casks', 'No.4688 & 5425', '...led in Scotland in 2018' (photo 1); '45,2 % vol.' and '1967 Tomint...' (photo 3); '70 cl.' on neck label and the Maryse Accorsi Samaroli tag text (photo 2). Confirmed: scan's text read is right, except the left of the label reads '1968' and the right '2018' around ANNIVERSARY. A second tag with a white panel reading 'Bottle ...' is visible behind the neck in photo 1; the bottle number is not readable. Refuted: the scan's 'fill into neck' cannot be judged through near-black glass, so fill is unknown, not confirmed. Capsule intact with a small nick or crease near the top edge (photo 3). Box present, plate engraving not legible.
lots.condition: Capsule intact (small nick at top edge), labels and tag clean, wooden box present. Fill not assessable through dark glass. Bottle number not legible.

lots.title: (1) McCallum's 'Perfection Scots Whisky' Blended Scotch Whisky, Scotland, 750ml, 42.3% ABV (Bottled in NZ)
lots.what_it_really_is: McCallum's Perfection Scots Whisky, D & J McCallum Ltd Edinburgh, bottled in New Zealand by The Distillers Co. (N.Z.) Ltd, Auckland, 750 ml, 42.3%, cream screw cap, Highlander front label and calligraphic back label. Metric 750 ml / 42.3% labelling points to a later NZ bottling (probably mid-1970s or later), not confirmed.
lots.what_the_title_misses: Nothing of value. Title gives brand, 750ml, 42.3% and Bottled in NZ. It omits the bottler name and screw cap, and gives no era, but the scan's 1957 to 1975 date from the 'century and a half' back-label wording is not reliable: that wording can persist for decades. A Canterbury Museum c.1960s NZ example is described with a gold-coloured lid and 74 proof, which differs from this cream-capped metric bottle, so this one is likely later than that.
lots.photo_evidence: Re-read all 3 photos and enlarged the lower front label (4x). Read: 'DISTILLED AND BLENDED IN SCOTLAND', 'McCallum's Perfection Scots Whisky', 'D & J McCallum Limited (FOUNDED 1807)', 'EDINBURGH', 'SCOTLAND', 'BOTTLED IN NEW ZEALAND THE DISTILLERS CO. (N.Z.) LTD., AUCKLAND', 'CONTENTS 750 ml', 'ALCOHOL CONTENT 42.3%'. Back label text confirmed as the scan read it. Cap reads 'McCallum's Perfection' and 'TURN'. Fill line sits in the lower neck, around the neck base (photo 3), consistent with the scan. Labels clean, no barcode visible on front or back. Scan text confirmed; scan dating inference not confirmed.
lots.condition: Screw cap intact, labels clean, fill in the lower neck / neck base.
lots.dropped_entries: All research entries dropped as not the same bottling: whisky.auction 51919 (page opened, GBP 210 winning bid, 12 Mar 2019, but 1950s bottle with no size or ABV on label and listed as 40%, so a different, older edition and over 24 months old); 88321 (page opened, 5cl miniature 1930s-40s, GBP 80, 25 Aug 2020); 66669, 66678, 66670 (66669 opened: 5cl 1930s, GBP 24, 22 Oct 2019; the others snippet only; miniatures); 184090 (page opened, 2 x 4.7cl 1930s US import, GBP 5 top bid, reserve not met, 30 Apr 2024); appraisily.com (generic AI-style guide range, not a sale or dealer price); Canterbury Museum 113240 (no price, page did not load, dating reference only). The research's GBP to NZD 2.20 rate was an assumption; actual 12 Oct 2026 rate is 2.3637.
lots.guide_summary: No sold, passed-in or asking price found for the NZ-bottled 750 ml 42.3% edition. The only full-bottle McCallum's result is an older 1950s bottle at GBP 210 in 2019 (about NZD 496 at today's rate), not comparable. Value likely modest, a niche NZ collectable.
lots.working: No same-bottling SOLD entry, so keep and flip are 0. Shipping NZ to Australia would add freight, duty and GST not included.
lots.confidence_reason: Label fully read, but no matching SOLD evidence.
lots.question_for_webbs: Any date code or embossing on the base of the bottle or glass, and a close photo of the cap seal to confirm it has not been opened.

lots.title: (1) Johnnie Walker Red Label Blended Scotch Whisky, Scotland, 750ml, 42.3% ABV (Bottled in NZ) (TOL) (MS)
lots.what_it_really_is: Johnnie Walker Red Label 'Old Scotch Whisky', 750 ml, 42.3%, bottled in New Zealand by The Distillers Co. (N.Z.) Ltd, Auckland, with Highest Awards base label, 'By Appointment to Her Majesty the Queen' neck label and gold and red screw cap. Metric 750 ml / 42.3% suggests late 1970s to 1980s; not confirmed.
lots.what_the_title_misses: Little. The title already says 750ml, 42.3%, Bottled in NZ, and flags label damage (TOL, consistent with the visible tear) and a fill note (MS). It omits the Queen's warrant neck label and Highest Awards strip, which are standard on Red Label of the era and add no clear value.
lots.photo_evidence: Re-read all 3 photos, enlarged the neck label (5x). Read: neck 'By Appointment to Her Majesty the Queen', 'Scotch Whisky Distillers', 'JOHN WALKER AND SONS LTD.'; front '...HOL CONTENT 42.3%', 'PRODUCE OF SCOTLAND', '750 ml', 'Johnnie Walker Red Old Scotch Whisky', 'JOHN WALKER & SONS LTD., KILMARNOCK, SCOTLAND', 'BOTTLED IN NEW ZEALAND THE DISTILLERS CO. (N.Z.) LTD., AUCK...'; base 'HIGHEST AWARDS' with Sydney 1880, Paris 1885, Adelaide 1887, Melbourne 1881, Dunedin, Jamaica, Kimberley, Brisbane (last digits cut off). Paper loss on the front label beside 'Red', front label slightly lifting at right. Partly refuted: the scan put the fill 'into base of neck'; photos 1 and 3 show the liquid line just below the neck label on the upper shoulder, not in the neck. Webb's MS note fits a shoulder fill better than the scan does.
lots.condition: Screw cap intact, front label paper loss (TOL), labels tarnished, fill at upper shoulder just under the neck label.
